title: A bulk change that partly fails lists the failed part and its reason
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create two active parts for this test, part A and part B.
  • Give parts A and B part numbers that start with the same text, so one search lists both.
  • Use a desktop browser that can open a second tab on the same ShopView address, signed in as the same user.
  • Start in tab 1 on the Inventory page, on the Active tab.
custom_steps:
1. Type the shared start of the part numbers in the Search box.
  2. Click the three-dot actions button (⋮) in the toolbar, to the left of New Inventory Part.
  3. Click Deactivate parts.
  4. Click the part A row.
  5. Click the part B row.
  6. Open a second browser tab on the same ShopView address.
  7. In tab 2, click Parts in the top bar.
  8. In tab 2, click Inventory in the left menu.
  9. In tab 2, type part B's part number in the Search box.
  10. In tab 2, click the part B row.
  11. In tab 2, click Inactive under Part Status.
  12. In tab 2, click Save.
  13. In tab 2, click Deactivate in the confirmation.
  14. Switch back to tab 1 without reloading it.
  15. Click Deactivate on the dark bar.
  16. Click Deactivate in the confirmation.
  17. Wait 10 seconds without closing the message.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Parts A and B are listed.

Step 2:

  • The menu opens.

Step 3:

  • Bulk mode turns on.

Step 4:

  • The part A row is ticked.

Step 5:

  • The bar reads 2 selected.

Step 6:

  • A second tab opens.

Step 7:

  • Tab 2 shows the Parts left menu.

Step 8:

  • Tab 2 shows the Inventory page.

Step 9:

  • Part B is listed in tab 2.

Step 10:

  • Edit Inventory Part opens for part B.

Step 11:

  • Inactive is picked.

Step 12:

  • The "Deactivate part?" confirmation opens.

Step 13:

  • Tab 2 shows "Part deactivated.": part B is now inactive.

Step 14:

  • Tab 1 still shows parts A and B ticked.

Step 15:

  • The "Deactivate parts?" confirmation reads "2 parts selected."

Step 16:

  • A red message reads "1 part updated, 1 could not be changed." and lists part B by its part number with the reason "Part is already in that state."
  • Part A leaves the Active tab; bulk mode stays on with only part B ticked (2 ticked = 1 changed + 1 failed).

Step 17:

  • The red message is still on screen after 10 seconds: it stays until closed.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10823 (Story 10, Confirming and Recording a Status Change), story SV-10815 (Story 2, Deactivate Parts in Bulk)

  • S10-R12: “After a bulk change, the system shows how many parts changed and how many failed.”
  • S10-R13: “For each part that failed, the system names the part by its number and gives the reason.”
  • S10-R13a: “The reasons are "A core follows its part. Activate or deactivate the part instead.", "Part not found." and "Part is already in that state."”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Bulk change, some parts failed | "{n} parts updated, {m} could not be changed." ("1 part updated, {m} could not be changed." for one) | Error toast, stays until closed, lists each failed part and its reason”
  • User Feedback Summary: “A part already in the requested state | "Part is already in that state." | Listed as the failure reason”
  • S2-R15: “When some parts fail, the mode stays on and the selection keeps only the parts that failed.”
